headline: Nvidia CEO sees $1 trillion of AI chip revenue opportunity through 2027
summary: STORY: :: Nvidia's CEO says he expects 'at least' $1 trillion in revenue from its newest AI chips through 2027:: San Jose, California / March 16, 2026:: Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO"AI is able to do productive work and therefore the inflection point of inference has arrived. AI now has to think, in order to think it has to inference. A.I. now has to do, in order to do it has to inference.  A.I. has to read, in order to do so, it has to inference. It has to reason. It has to inference. Every part of AI, every time that it has to think, it has to reason, it has to do, it has to generate tokens, it has to inference. It's way past training now. It's in the field of inference. So the inference inflection has arrived. // I'm here to tell you that right now, where I stand a few short months after GTC DC, one year after last GTC, right here where I stand, I see through 2027 at least $1 trillion."At its annual GTC developer conference in San Jose, California, Nvidia unveiled a new central processor and an AI system built on technology from startup Groq - part of CEO Jensen Huang’s push to strengthen the company’s position in so-called inference computing.Inference poses greater competition for Nvidia including from custom processors built by customers such as Meta, even as it dominates the market for chips used to train AI with its graphics processors.

headline: Nvidia's Huang says AI will create jobs, not cut them
summary: STORY: :: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says AI will create more jobs, not eliminate them:: San Jose, California / March 17, 2026"A lot of people say AI's coming, we're going to run out of our work, our jobs. It's exactly the opposite. The fact of the matter is PCs made us more busy. The internet made us more busy, mobile devices made us super busy.""We are millions of truck drivers short. We are tens of millions of manufacturing workers short. Employment is very high and yet many companies don't have enough labor, most companies don't have enough labor.  Robots will fill in that gap, number one. As a result of filling that gap, all of our countries' economy will grow. And when the economy grows most companies tend to hire more people. They'll hire more people, to manage more robots. Hire more people to manage more agents.":: Huang also pledged his support for Nvidia teams in Israel and Taiwan"We have 6000 families in Israel and I'm quite worried about them. I know that they're worried about themselves. I'm 100% committed to Israel where we are going to be there for a very long time and 100% of our employees there, they have 100% of our love and support. That is 100% also true about Taiwan. We have several thousand employees there. They've been there a very long time. Huang said AI systems, including autonomous agents, will require human oversight and management, ultimately driving hiring rather than reducing it.Huang outlined a future in which Nvidia's workforce operates alongside millions of AI agents working continuously.Huang also addressed geopolitical concerns affecting Nvidia's global workforce, particularly in Israel and Taiwan.During the Q&A, Huang also received the 2026 MotorTrend Person of the Year award, an honor previously given to Elon Musk.

headline: Baidu debuts AI 'Lobsters' as Nvidia CEO hails OpenClaw
summary: STORY: Lobsters were everywhere at an event hosted by China's leading internet search provider, Baidu, in Beijing this week. It introduced a family of "lobsters," its nickname for AI agents built on OpenClaw, an open source tool.Reuters Correspondent Stephen Nellis covers the technology industry and attended Nvidia’s recent conference where OpenClaw was a hot topic."One way to think about this thing called OpenClaw is a sort of middle management layer for AI employees. So in the AI world, there are these things called agents that act like employees that can go out and use a piece of software for you or carry out a task."(FLASH)"So OpenClaw acts like a bit of a middle manager where you tell the computer what you want done, and then it goes and finds the right employees, the right agents to go carry out that task. It collects all that information and then brings it back to you in language that humans can understand."Think trip planning or pulling together a project.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang called the technology “the next ChatGPT” and (quote) "the most popular open source project in the history of humanity.”"OpenClaw has open-sourced essentially the operating system of agentic computers. It is no different than how Windows made it possible for us to create personal computers. Now, OpenClaw has made it possible for us to create personal agents."Growing enthusiasm over the technology sent Chinese tech shares up by as much as 22% in recent weeks as companies rolled out a suite of products based on the agent.“this is stunningly exciting”Former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger sees tremendous potential for the concept but a lot of risks too."OpenClaw's, you know, a couple months old, right? We're barely in this view of how agents are going to get deployed and operationalized. And of course, businesses are lookin g at this a couple of months old. And there's tons of security issues, right. There's a lot of questions of, how do I get access to my data? How do I make it available to my enterprise systems? How secure is it when I've done that?”Companies like Nvidia are already working on this. It is targeting the autonomous AI agent market through NemoClaw, an add‑on system that integrates with OpenClaw to provide privacy and safety controls for AI agents capable of executing a wide range of tasks with minimal human oversight.
